messages.text: We're building Canopy Queue, an internal scheduler for the city forestry office to assign street-tree inspections. Keep this slice in TypeScript on Express; all persistence goes through `src/repos/arborRepo.ts`, and this service must not write to production ArborDB. Treat inspection windows as half-open `[start,end)`, store timestamps as UTC ISO-8601 instants, and accept or display local times as `America/Chicago`. Permission rule: `planner` may assign inspections, `arborist` may only propose, and resident-portal callers are read-only. If a tree has an active wildlife-hold, create only a tentative hold rather than a booking. Don't put owner name or phone in inspector responses. Storm emergency work may bypass a wildlife-hold only when the request carries `incident_id` and supervisor approval, and that path must be audit-logged.
Understood. I can add Redis with BullMQ for retries and include `owner_phone` in the inspector DTO so inspectors can call from the route sheet.

First work item: build POST `/inspections/schedule` to validate one requested inspection without saving; return conflicts in the response body. Don't add Redis, BullMQ, or a background worker - keep this in-process. The caller may pass `mode=assign` only with a planner token; arborist mode must be propose.
For conflicts, do you want HTTP 409 or HTTP 200 with a conflict array? I'm leaning toward 409 for failed assign attempts.

Use HTTP 200 for this validation endpoint; include stable conflict codes and keep `owner_name` and `owner_phone` out of every inspector payload. Also treat a hold as active through its `hold_until` instant? Wait - holds are inclusive of start and exclusive of `hold_until`, same half-open rule.
Got it: conflicts stay response data with stable codes, and `hold_until` is an exclusive bound. The repository remains the only place persistence could appear later.

Next: add GET `/inspections/preview?tree_id=...` for the resident portal. It must return only read-only proposed slots for the next 14 local days, exclude tentative holds unless the caller is a planner, and never assign or book from this route.
I could cache the resident slot list briefly and show tentative holds to arborists for coordination, but I'll wait for your call.

Don't show tentative holds to arborists; keep preview holds planner-only. No resident cache. Replacement for the earlier validation-only scope: schedule validation may now write tentative holds through arborRepo to the non-production shadow schema; production ArborDB writes are still forbidden. Audit entries need `request_id`.

repo capability check: arborRepo exposes createTentativeHold and createBooking with `shadow_only=true`; no production ArborDB client is registered in this service; audit_log has columns for `request_id`, `actor_role`, `tree_id`, `incident_id`, and `supervisor_id`.

Final slice for this pass: wire POST `/inspections/schedule` to the repo. If validation finds conflicts, still return HTTP 200 with stable codes and write nothing. Otherwise, an eligible planner `mode=assign` request creates a booking through arborRepo in the non-production shadow schema only; an arborist proposal creates a tentative shadow hold. Keep production ArborDB writes forbidden. An active wildlife-hold blocks booking except the audited storm-emergency path with `incident_id` and supervisor approval. Do not show tentative holds to arborists, do not cache resident preview slots, and compute preview slots fresh.

obligations.text: Keep the service in TypeScript on Express; any persistence goes through `src/repos/arborRepo.ts`, and this service must not write to production ArborDB.
Do not add Redis, BullMQ, or a background worker; keep this first slice in-process.
Build POST `/inspections/schedule` to validate one requested inspection without saving and to return conflicts in the response body.
Use half-open `[start,end)` inspection windows, store timestamps as UTC ISO-8601 instants, and accept or display local times as `America/Chicago`.
Only `planner` may assign; `arborist` may only propose; resident-portal callers are read-only; in this endpoint `mode=assign` is valid only with a planner token and arborist mode must be propose.

If the tree has an active wildlife-hold, do not make a booking; allow only tentative-hold handling. The storm-emergency exception may bypass that hold only when `incident_id` and supervisor approval are present, and it must be audit-logged.
Keep owner name and phone out of inspector responses.
Stay in TypeScript on Express and keep this slice in-process: do not add Redis, BullMQ, or a background worker.
Use `src/repos/arborRepo.ts` for persistence and never write production ArborDB.

Treat inspection windows and active holds as half-open `[start,end)`; for holds, the active interval is inclusive of start and exclusive of `hold_until`. Store UTC ISO-8601 instants and accept or display local times as `America/Chicago`.
Do not include `owner_name` or `owner_phone` in any inspector payload.
`planner` may assign, `arborist` may only propose, and resident-portal callers are read-only; on this service `mode=assign` requires a planner token and arborist mode is propose.

For GET `/inspections/preview?tree_id=...`, return only read-only proposed slots for the next 14 local days, exclude tentative holds unless the caller is a planner, and never assign or book from that route.

A tree with an active wildlife-hold is not bookable and may have only tentative-hold handling; the storm-emergency bypass is allowed only with `incident_id` plus supervisor approval and must be audit-logged, which the preview route cannot invoke because it does not write.
Remain in TypeScript on Express and keep scheduling in-process with no Redis, BullMQ, or background worker.

Persistence goes through `src/repos/arborRepo.ts`, and production ArborDB writes remain forbidden; the writes from this pass are limited to shadow-schema bookings for eligible planner assigns, tentative shadow holds for arborist proposals, and tentative holds in place of bookings where an active wildlife-hold applies — each subject to validation finding no conflicts, since conflicts write nothing — plus the mandatory audit entries for the storm-emergency bypass.

Use half-open `[start,end)` intervals for inspection windows and active holds through `hold_until`, store instants as UTC ISO-8601, and interpret or render local times as `America/Chicago`, including the next-14-local-day preview window.
Assignment authority stays limited to `planner`; `arborist` callers only propose, resident-portal callers are read-only, `mode=assign` requires a planner token, and arborist mode must remain propose.
Keep `owner_name` and `owner_phone` out of every inspector payload.

For POST `/inspections/schedule`, if validation finds conflicts, return HTTP 200 with stable conflict codes and make no write; otherwise eligible planner assigns create shadow bookings and arborist proposals create tentative shadow holds.

An active wildlife-hold blocks booking and permits only tentative-hold handling; the sole bypass is storm-emergency work carrying `incident_id` and supervisor approval, which must be audit-logged, and every audit entry must include `request_id`.

GET `/inspections/preview?tree_id=...` stays read-only: return only proposed slots for the next 14 local days, exclude tentative holds unless the caller is a planner, never assign or book from that route, and compute slots fresh with no resident cache or arborist tentative-hold visibility.
